clue.text: Undercook or marinate no end — check beef regularly

indicators.note: with no end means the final letter of the synonym for marinate is dropped

parts.note: to souse food is to steep or marinate it in pickle
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of beef is taken, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: steep the beef, or check on it every so often while cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undercook' is not about cooking too little: it means the cook under the head chef.
explanation.definitionFit: A sous-chef is the second-in-command in a professional kitchen, literally an under-cook.

clue.text: Hunter's prayer has not succeeded

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: has not means the letter for succeeded is missing from the prayer

parts.note: an orison is an old word for a prayer
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A hunter whose prayers went unanswered.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the mythical giant huntsman, now a constellation.

clue.text: Swimmers in teams chasing second place

indicators.note: chasing means the teams come after second place in the answer

parts.note: second place earns a silver medal
sides are teams in a match

explanation.surface: Swimmers in relay teams pushing to take the silver medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Silversides are small fish with a silvery stripe, so they are swimmers in the sea.

clue.text: What do you think of a fight after hours that hurt?

indicators.note: after places the fight later in the answer than the other pieces

parts.note: ow is the cry of someone hurt
a bout is a boxing fight

explanation.surface: Someone asks your opinion of a painful late-night brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases invite someone's opinion of a suggestion, as in asking for a view on a plan.

clue.text: Find her at feeder, flapping?

indicators.note: flapping suggests wings beating wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Look for her at the bird feeder, wings flapping.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a bird found at a feeder, flapping its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy idiom for a bird, the kind of visitor seen flapping at a garden feeder.

clue.text: Unknown enemy dispersing: that can bring a reaction

indicators.note: dispersing means scattering, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious enemy scatters, which might provoke a response.
explanation.definitionFit: Enzymes are biological catalysts that bring about chemical reactions in living things.

clue.text: Measuring device minus top still standing

indicators.note: minus top means the first letter is taken off, in a down clue the top one

parts.note: a sextant is a navigator's instrument for measuring angles

explanation.surface: An old instrument, missing its top, still survives.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extant still exists, having survived, like a building still standing.

clue.text: Man of paradox omits nothing in branch of religion

indicators.note: omits means the letter for nothing is left out

parts.note: Zeno of Elea is the Greek philosopher famed for his paradoxes
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A paradoxical thinker leaves nothing out of his religious school.
explanation.definitionFit: Zen is a school of Buddhism, so a branch of one religion.

clue.text: Dreary strips gone over in race

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the race

parts.note: the mile is a running race

indicators.note: gone over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to bare is to strip, so strips gives bares

explanation.surface: A dull report: athletes strip off after the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone over' reads the synonym for strips backwards; the mile is a classic athletics distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable weather or company is gloomy and depressing, i.e. dreary.

clue.text: Part of face turned down, on this?

definitions.text: Part of face turned down, on this?

indicators.note: turned means read the other way round

parts.note: the lip is part of the face
low means down, as in feeling low

explanation.surface: Where you lay your face down when you sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a face is turned down onto a pillow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion for the head in bed, on which a sleeper's face rests turned down.

clue.text: "Villa's other half is hotel" shock

parts.note: the football club Aston Villa: the other half of its name is Aston
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about a footballer's partner and a hotel scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club; 'other half' sounds like a spouse but means the rest of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock or stun someone is to amaze them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Anxious to put name forward for bender

indicators.note: put, with forward, says a letter is moved earlier in the word
forward says the letter for name moves towards the front

parts.note: keen means eager, anxious to do something

explanation.surface: Someone eager to propose a name for a drinking session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bender' looks like a binge; it is a joint that bends.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint in the middle of the leg is what lets it bend, so a bender.

clue.text: Responsible for some music not being free

parts.note: to be behind a scheme is to be responsible for it
bars are short sections of music

explanation.surface: A composer credited with a few bars of a song who is not free.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being in prison, locked up and so lacking freedom.

clue.text: I ask for a bun, rambling in the country

indicators.note: rambling means wandering aimlessly, so these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A rambler out walking in the countryside asks for a bun.
explanation.definitionFit: Burkina Faso is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Short skirmish in France that resistance can make shorter

indicators.note: short means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a brush is a brief clash or skirmish
que is the French for that
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A brief skirmish in wartime France that the Resistance could cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like the definition, but it trims BRUSH; 'can make' links to 'shorter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brusquer is the comparative of brusque, meaning more curt or abrupt in manner.

clue.text: Fit pair of spectacles worn by N European hunchback

parts.note: to rig is to fit out, as with a ship

indicators.note: worn by means the spectacles wrap around the European

parts.note: the two round lenses of spectacles look like two letters O
a Lett is a Latvian, from northern Europe

explanation.surface: A north European hunchback is fitted with a pair of glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lett is a native of Latvia; the two round lenses become two Os, one on each side of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is the hunchbacked jester in Verdi's opera of that name.

clue.text: King putting medal on official dress

indicators.note: putting on means the king is set before the medal
putting on means the king is set before the medal

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
the OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A monarch pins a medal onto ceremonial dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long formal gown worn by judges or peers as dress of office.

clue.text: As creator, stick in more purple

indicators.note: in means the stick goes inside the colour word

parts.note: puce is a purplish-brown, so pucer is more purple
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: An artist adds a stick to deepen the purple.
explanation.definitionFit: A producer is a maker, one who brings something into being.

clue.text: My word once accepted by renegade

indicators.note: accepted by means held inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise from a turncoat's admission.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, like 'my word', now dated.

clue.text: To be off the track could be deadlier

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form another word when reordered

explanation.surface: A train leaving the rails might be even more lethal.
explanation.definitionFit: A derailed train has left its rails, so it is literally off the line.

clue.text: With long, awkward limbs in aisle, left for Washington

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in place of another

parts.note: a gangway is a passage between seats, an aisle
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: A lanky person sprawled in the aisle, heading left for Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use a gangway is the passage between rows of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangly person is tall and thin with ungainly arms and legs.

clue.text: The lead is mine, as hearts and diamonds are unlucky

parts.note: saying I will take the lead role means I'll star
hearts and diamonds are the red suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A card player claims the lead, as the red suits turn out unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-starred means doomed by bad fortune, as though born under an evil star.

clue.text: A fish makes one helping

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called orfe

explanation.surface: A fish makes one portion at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like a portion of food; it means assisting.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is someone who helps, so an aide is one helping.

clue.text: Raise a few daughters, or masses

indicators.note: raise in a down clue means the letters are turned upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: some means a few
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Bringing up a few daughters, or a great many children.
explanation.definitionFit: The demos is the populace, the common people of a state.

clue.text: Society figure not one to suppress

indicators.note: not means the letter for one is absent

parts.note: a triangle is a geometric figure
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A high-society personality who refuses to hush things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle a plan or a sound is to stifle it, crush it before it grows.

clue.text: Out of hospital, listen to chest

indicators.note: out of means the hospital letter departs from the word

parts.note: hark is an old command meaning listen

explanation.surface: A discharged patient has a doctor listen to their chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' suggests the body; it is a box.
explanation.definitionFit: An ark is an old word for a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant.

clue.text: Big gaps in a text used by church

indicators.note: used by places the church ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: an SMS is a text message

explanation.surface: Gaps in a passage of scripture as read by the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasms are deep fissures, so big gaps in the ground or figuratively.

clue.text: Struggle for position in clubs toured by comic

indicators.note: toured by means the comic word goes round the clubs letter

parts.note: jokey means funny, comic
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A stand-up comedian on a tour of clubs, jostling to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To jockey is to manoeuvre for advantage, as riders do in a race.

clue.text: Sleeping place has no value for little creature

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a sleeping place
O is zero, none
use means value, as in of no use

explanation.surface: A dormitory dismissed as worthless for a small animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse is a small hibernating rodent, a tiny furry animal.
